tagline.en: Salt Lake City's Belt Route, sunk below its neighbours
tagline.zh: 盐湖城环线：沉入街区之下

mileageSource: FHWA Route Log and Finder List, Table 2, January 2026

start.en: I-80 at the mouth of Parley's Canyon, east of Salt Lake City
start.zh: 盐湖城以东帕利峡谷口，与 I-80 相接

end.zh: 北盐湖城，与 I-15 相接

en: I-215 is the Belt Route around Salt Lake City: an arc from I-80 at the mouth of Parley's Canyon in the east, south through Holladay and Murray, west past the airport and north to I-15 at North Salt Lake. I-15 and I-80 complete the ring through the middle of the city. The western two-thirds let through traffic and airport traffic bypass the centre; the south-eastern leg is a commuter road serving Cottonwood Heights and Holladay.

What is distinctive about it is how much of it is below grade. Where the freeway runs through established residential areas UDOT depressed it and built concrete noise walls, a compromise reached with the neighbourhoods that fought it. The section completed in July 1985 between 280 East and Union Park Avenue was, at the time, the most expensive road per mile ever built in Utah, for precisely that reason.
zh: I-215 是环绕盐湖城的「环线」：自东侧帕利峡谷口的 I-80 起画一道弧，南下穿过霍拉迪与默里，向西经过机场，再北上接到北盐湖城的 I-15。穿城而过的 I-15 与 I-80 补齐了这个环。西侧三分之二让过境交通与机场交通绕开市中心；东南段则是服务棉木高地与霍拉迪的通勤道路。
它的特别之处在于有多大比例低于地面。凡是穿过成熟居住区的地方，犹他州交通部都把高速下沉并修建混凝土声屏障——这是与反对它的社区达成的妥协。1985 年 7 月建成的 280 East 至联合公园大道段，正因如此，在当时是犹他州历来每英里造价最高的道路。

en: The belt was proposed in the mid-1950s with I-15 and I-80, but as two roads: the western quadrant was I-215 and the eastern portion was I-415. Utah petitioned AASHO on 14 October 1968 to give the whole loop one number, and from 1969 it was all I-215. The plan was for nine sections costing $65 million, finished by 1974. The first piece opened by 1963 as a two-lane road linking 2100 North with Redwood Road to improve access to the airport.

Then it stopped. Residents of the neighbourhoods in the path — including the painter Arnold Friberg — fought the road, community groups took it to court, environmental law changed under it, and the litigation held up completion by at least ten years. UDOT eventually bought and demolished about 150 homes. The western quadrant was finished on 7 October 1988 with a 3.2-mile, six-lane section costing $36.6 million, and the belt was closed in October 1989 when the stretch between 4500 South and 6200 South opened, the last leg of a $38 million project. Governor Norm Bangerter dedicated it.
zh: 这条环线在 1950 年代中期与 I-15、I-80 一并提出，但当时是两条路：西象限为 I-215，东段为 I-415。犹他州于 1968 年 10 月 14 日向美国州公路工作者协会申请给整个环线统一编号，自 1969 年起全线改称 I-215。原定分九段施工、造价 6,500 万美元、1974 年完工。首段在 1963 年前通车，是一条连接 2100 North 与红木路的双车道道路，用于改善机场通行。

然后就停了。沿线街区的居民——包括画家阿诺德·弗里伯格——起而反对，社区团体把它告上法庭，环境法规在此期间发生变化，诉讼至少把工期拖后了十年。犹他州交通部最终收购并拆除了约 150 栋住宅。西象限于 1988 年 10 月 7 日随一段 3.2 英里、六车道、造价 3,660 万美元的路段完工；1989 年 10 月，4500 South 与 6200 South 之间路段通车，环线合圈，这是一个 3,800 万美元项目的最后一段。诺姆·班格特州长为其主持通车仪式。

timeline.en: The first piece of the belt opens near the airport.
timeline.zh: 环线首段在机场附近通车。

timeline.en: The eastern I-415 designation is dropped and the whole loop becomes I-215.
timeline.zh: 东段 I-415 编号撤销，整个环线统一为 I-215。

timeline.en: The depressed section between 280 East and Union Park Avenue opens, the costliest road per mile in Utah at the time.
timeline.zh: 280 East 至联合公园大道的下沉路段通车，为当时犹他州每英里造价最高的道路。

timeline.en: The last section opens in October, fifteen years later than planned.
timeline.zh: 最后一段于 10 月通车，比原定计划晚了十五年。
